An Aspirational Community That Enjoys Learning and Contributes to an Ever-Changing World
At Perivale Primary School, we aim to inspire, enthuse and ignite a lifelong passion for learning in every child. Our curriculum is ambitious, engaging and inclusive, providing children with the knowledge, skills and experiences they need to thrive both now and in the future.
Our school values are at the heart of everything we do. They are the foundation of our curriculum and shape the way our children learn, grow and interact with the world around them.
Through our curriculum, we encourage pupils to be curious, confident, resilient and aspirational, empowering them to achieve their very best and make a positive contribution to an ever-changing world.
Our Vision and Values
At Perivale Primary School, our values sit at the heart of everything we do. Alongside the fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs, we aim to inspire every child to aspire to be the very best they can be.
We want our pupils to grow into confident, respectful and responsible individuals who are well prepared for their future and empowered to make a positive contribution to their local community and the wider world.
Collaboration is an important part of our school culture. We work closely with one another, our families, our community and partner schools to share good practice, learn together and continually strive for excellence.

Welcome to Perivale Primary School
Thank you for visiting our website and welcome to Perivale Primary School. We are a two-form community school for children aged 3 to 11, located in the suburb of Ealing, West London. We pride ourselves on providing a happy, safe and nurturing environment for children as we prepare them for secondary school and beyond. Our long serving staff ensure we know our community well and that links between school and families are strong.
Perivale is a friendly school with a strong, nurturing and caring ethos. We have an amazing team of dedicated staff who passionately strive to ensure that all children aspire to be the best they can be. Staff work collaboratively to ensure the best possible outcomes for children.
Our ambition is for children to leave our school academically successful and as positive, happy individuals who embody our core values. Developing the whole child and equipping them with positive learning behaviours, attitudes and values are central to our approach. We expect excellent behaviour from our children at all times of the school day and have a clear, simple behaviour policy to help them with this. We value respect, manners and good behaviour.
Our curriculum is vibrant and creative. Children are encouraged to explore, discover and question through a range of exciting learning opportunities both within and outside the classroom, including extra-curricular activities, with an aim of fulfilling their future aspirations.
I hope you enjoy finding out more about our school by browsing our website. Visits are encouraged and warmly welcomed; we would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school.
Daniel UpfieldHeadteacher

SEND and Inclusion
SEND & Inclusion at Perivale Primary School
At Perivale Primary School, we are committed to creating an inclusive learning environment where every child, regardless of their needs, can thrive. As a mainstream primary school, we recognize and celebrate the diverse abilities of all our pupils and are dedicated to providing high-quality support tailored to individual needs.
Our approach aligns with the Equality Act 2010 and the SEND Code of Practice (2015), ensuring that children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) receive the right support to access a broad and balanced curriculum.
Working in Partnership with Parents
We firmly believe that collaboration with parents and carers is key to ensuring the best outcomes for our children. We work closely with families every step of the way, valuing their expertise and unique insight into their child’s needs. Through regular communication, workshops, and meetings, we create strong partnerships that empower parents to be active participants in their child’s learning journey.
We also collaborate with a range of external professionals, including Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, School Counsellors, Ealing Primary Centre, SEND Outreach, and Educational Psychologists, to ensure a holistic approach to support.
Our Provision
To meet the needs of all learners, we offer:
We encourage families to explore their Local Offer, which provides comprehensive information on services and support available to children and young people with SEND:
For further resources and updates, please visit our Padlet: The PPP where you will find useful guidance, strategies, and support networks.

Supporting Transitions at Perivale Primary School
At Perivale Primary School, we recognize that transitions—whether into our school, within the school day, or onto a new setting—can be a significant time for children and their families. We are committed to carefully planning and supporting each transition to ensure every child feels confident, secure, and ready for the next step in their learning journey
Starting at Perivale Primary School
We work closely with families and previous settings to gather key information about each child’s needs, strengths, and support strategies. This includes:
Transitions Within the School Day
We understand that smaller daily transitions—such as moving between activities, lessons, or environments—can be challenging for some children. To support this, we use:
Moving to a New Setting
When children transition to secondary school or another setting, we work closely with families and the receiving school to ensure a well-planned and supportive process, which may include:
By prioritising communication, careful planning, and individualised approaches, we ensure that all transitions—big or small—are positive experiences that set children up for success.
What Should I Do If I Have Concerns?
If you have concerns about your child’s development, learning, or well-being and feel they may need additional help, support, or assessment, we encourage you to speak with us. Our SEND and Inclusion Team is here to listen, provide guidance, and work with you to explore the best strategies and interventions to meet your child’s needs. We strongly believe that early identification and support are key, and we are committed to working in partnership with parents to ensure every child receives the right level of support to reach their full potential.
Please don’t hesitate to contact the school to arrange a conversation—we are here to help.

Phonics and Early Reading
Phonics and Early Reading
SEND and Inclusion
Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised Programme Progression
How phonics is taught at Perivale Primary Primary
Phonics is taught using the Systematic Synthetic Phonics Programme, Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised.
Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised has been developed by Wandle and Little Sutton English Hubs and taken forward by Little Sutton Primary School and Wandle Learning Trust in partnership with other phonics and early reading experts. The Systematic Synthetic Phonics programme draws on the latest research into how children learn best; how to ensure learning stays in children’s long-term memory and how best to enable children to apply their learning to become highly competent readers.
To learn more about the programme, please click on the link: Little Wandle
The resources on the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised page will help you support your child with saying their sounds and writing their letters. There are also some useful videos so you can see how they are taught at school and feel confident about supporting their reading at home.

Beyond the classroom – Residentials
‘An aspirational community that enjoys learning and contributes to an ever-changing world’
We are: Resilient Respectful Curious Inclusive
Residential Journeys
We believe that residential trips offer invaluable experiences that contribute to the personal and social development of our students. These visits provide opportunities for children to build independence, develop resilience, and form stronger bonds with their peers and teachers.
Benefits of Residential Trips:
We are proud to offer annual residential journeys for our Year 6 pupils. These residential educational visits are packed with exciting activities like abseiling, canoeing, and zip-lining, providing a thrilling and educational experience that students look forward to every year.
In addition to off-site residential trips, in Key stage 2 we also offer an onsite residential camping experience. This unique opportunity allows students to enjoy the excitement of camping while staying within the familiar surroundings of our school grounds. Our onsite camping includes activities such as team-building exercises, outdoor games, and campfire storytelling, providing a fun and safe environment for students to explore and grow.
We believe in exploring opportunities beyond our school’s walls to broaden our student’s horizons and elevate their aspirations. We expect all pupils to participate in our residential visits to foster a strong sense of community. We are committed to working with parents to overcome any barriers to participation. Together, we can create unforgettable experiences that inspire and empower our students.

Student Leadership
At Perivale Primary School we work hard to ensure everyone has a voice – especially the students!
We listen to what our children think, what our children say and their suggestions to make our school better. Students are the biggest part of our school community and at Perivale we provide them lots of opportunities to represent our school, to have their say and to bring about positive change. We also believe that leadership skills, even at a young age, are extremely important for the children to develop. This will allow them to succeed in later life and prepare them for life beyond primary school.
Many of our student leadership activities focus on improving the quality of teaching and learning in the classroom, taking part in student-led change initiatives and supporting the school’s vision to be ‘an aspirational community that enjoys learning and contributes to an ever-changing world.’
The aims of our student leadership programme are simple:
There are many leadership opportunities available to students, below is a flavour of what is currently on offer.
Extra-Curricular
Educational Visits
Residentials
Student Leadership
Head Boy and Head Girl
At the start of Year 6, all of the children are given the opportunity to apply for the position of Head Boy or Head Girl. They are asked to write a letter of application based on the following job description: Head Girl and Head Boy – Job Specification.
From the letters received, children are shortlisted for a formal interview, including a presentation component. The final 3 boys and final 3 girls then carry out an election campaign with a subsequent whole school vote at ballot stations.
Our Head Boy and Head Girl are ambassadors for our school, greeting formal visitors to the school and promoting our school value of RESPECT and upholding the highest of standards at all times – embodying our school values. At Perivale, they are also involved in recruitment and helped during the interviews to appoint members of our school community, recently some of our new SMSAs. They introduced a staff wellbeing initiative called ‘Pat on the Back’ and regularly lead key stage and whole school assemblies. These children are also the leaders of ‘Perivale Parliament’ and alongside Miss MacKenzie, one of our Assistant Headteachers, create agendas and lead the Parliament meetings.
We also have two fantastic deputy Head Boy and Head Girls who work as part of the Head Boy and Girl team to run many of our whole school initiatives.
Perivale Parliament
Our Perivale Parliament includes students from Year 1 – Year 6 who sit on our school parliament. Each meeting has a clear agenda and children have a record book to keep track of their agendas, actions and information to take back to class. Perivale Parliament have run a number of very successful events this year including – World Kindness Day, Remembrance Day and were heavily involved in Children’s Mental Health Week.
During our meetings, students bring ideas for improvement areas from their peers and then can feedback in class the outcomes of the discussions. From the ideas gathered at the beginning of the school year, we created an action plan that we are working through to focus on school improvement.
A full job description can be found here: Perivale Parliament – Job Specification.
Team Captains
At Perivale Primary School, we have 5 core learning values – We are ‘RESPECTFUL’, we are ‘INCLUSIVE’, We are ‘CURIOUS’, We are ‘RESILIENT’ and We ‘AIM HIGH’. Each of the houses are represented by a famous person as below.
Malala House (Resilient) – Malala Yousef
Peake House (Aim High) – Tim Peake
Hawking House (Curious) – Stephen Hawking
Elizabeth House (Respectful) – Queen Elizabeth
Mandela House (Inclusive) – Nelson Mandela
We have elected 3 team captains per house who are responsible for organising team events, collecting team points and announcing winners in the weekly assembly. For each house, there are 3 team captains; two children from Key Stage 2 and a younger KS1 child who shadows and learns leadership skills.
These positions are appointed through a class vote.
Healthy Eating Ambassadors
We have a small team of children who have a passion for healthy foods and healthy eating. They run a number of whole school events to promote healthy eating including leading a whole school assembly and organising events for our Healthy Eating Week. They have regular monthly meetings with our ISS manager, who provides our catering, to give feedback directly from the student body on the improvements that may need to be made around school lunches.
Playground Leaders
Our Playground Leaders are an elected group of children from upper Key Stage 2, who are involved in supporting cooperative play on the playground. Our Playground leaders with staff help devise simple playground games. This group of children also run our school ‘Tuck Shop’ which is the way that we distribute resources at lunchtimes for example: cricket sets, footballs and skipping ropes. They ensure that resources are signed out, returned and the resources are neatly maintained.
Wellbeing Warriors
Our newest student leadership opportunity is the Wellbeing Warriors. We have 8 members of year 5 and 6 and the children collaborate with each other to set up events and activities to support communities through fundraising, communication and acts of service. These communities range from the local area of Perivale, our school community and even individual year groups. The children will build social and communication skills as well as confidence through this group as they share their news with the school body in assemblies.
Travel Explorers
Our travel explorers are a group of year 4 and 5 students who were chosen to promote sustainable travel. The children are involved in and plan events that entice our school community to walk more and drive less. The children are aware that the more cars on the road the more pollution everyone in our school is exposed to. The children are actively involved in walk to school events, class competitions and auditing our school to allow us to move forward.

Premises Hire
We are proud to be able to offer many of our facilities for use by our community. Facilities available for community lettings include the school halls, Classrooms, Conference room and a large field.

Viewing Request

Safeguarding
Where the school hires or rents out the facilities/premises to organisations or individuals (for example to community groups, sports associations, and service providers to run community or extra-curricular activities) they should ensure that appropriate arrangements are in place to keep children safe.
When services or activities are provided under the direct supervision or management of the school or staff, these arrangements are managed under the school’s child protection and Safeguarding policy.

Discover, Learn & Have Fun!
At Perivale Primary School, we offer a fantastic range of clubs and activities to inspire every child. Our after-school clubs give pupils the opportunity to try something new, discover their talents, build confidence and develop new skills – all while having fun with their friends.
From sports and creativity to cooking, technology and much more, there’s something for everyone to enjoy!
Join the fun! Take a look at some of the exciting after-school clubs we offer:
Football Club: An invite-only club for selected pupils, led by our specialist football coach. Children develop their football skills, teamwork and confidence through focused, high-quality coaching, with opportunities to represent the school and compete in fixtures against other schools throughout the year.
Cooking Club: Delivered by My Little Chef At Home, this fun and hands-on club gives children the chance to get creative in the kitchen while developing valuable life skills. Children explore sweet and savoury dishes, learn about nutrition and build confidence, independence, teamwork, creativity, literacy and numeracy – all while having lots of fun! Sessions are available for Years 1–6, with a trial class for just £5. Interest-free split payment options are also available. Bookings & Enquiries: Parents can find out more and book directly through My Little Chef At Home.
Book with My Little Chef At Home
K-Kwon-Do: A fun and energetic martial arts club designed to help children develop confidence, discipline, fitness and self-defence skills in a supportive environment. Classes are suitable for children aged 4 years and above and take place every Monday from 3:15pm–4:15pm at Perivale Primary School. The first class is free, and sibling discounts are available. Bookings & Enquiries: Parents can contact Master Bushra Khosla, 6th Degree Black Belt and Director/Founder, directly to register or find out more. Tel: 07843 053076
Email: bushrakhosla@yahoo.co.ukK-Kwon-Do website
Active Champions Clubs: Delivered by Active Champions, our exciting after-school programme offers Gymnastics, STEM and Art clubs throughout the week. Children can learn new skills, build confidence, make friends and have fun in engaging sessions led by experienced coaches. Bookings & Enquiries: Parents can book directly with Active Champions online. Use discount code PERIVALE10 for 10% sibling discount.

Responsibilities of the Governing Body
The Governing Body is dedicated to promoting high standards of educational achievement at the school. As the accountable body, it provides strategic direction by establishing a vision and defining the school’s purpose and aims within an agreed policy framework. The Governing Body diligently monitors and evaluates the school’s performance and the effectiveness of the school improvement plan. Additionally, the Governing Body acts as a ‘critical friend,’ offering both support and constructive challenge to the senior leadership team
What is Governance?
When do the Governors meet?
The Governing Body convenes six times a year, once each half term, as a Full Governing Body. The Governors come from diverse backgrounds, bringing a wide range of skills to the table. This diversity, coupled with their shared commitment to the pupils and staff, contributes significantly to their success.
Key Responsibilities:
These responsibilities ensure that school governors play a crucial role in the governance and success of the school.

Aims
The Perivale curriculum is the planned experiences and interactions our children encounter every day. It aims to develop curious and confident learners and provide all pupils with opportunities to achieve high standards. It is designed to develop a capacity to accommodate new knowledge, always building on prior knowledge and experiences. At Perivale, your child’s learning is taken from the National Curriculum and a locally agreed syllabus for religious education.
The teaching of our curriculum is complemented by a wide selection of resources such as Chromebooks, mathematical equipment and a wide range of texts in English. We utilise the skills of our teachers to inspire all of our pupils to achieve their full potential. We value cross curricular learning, and we create strong links between core and non-core subjects by closely assessing which skills each academic discipline requires and finding the points of crossover.
Implementation
In designing our curriculum, we have a dual focus on what children should be learning and how best to teach it. In making decisions about what to teach, we first ensure that all National Curriculum requirements are covered, and then draw on elements of exceptional practice from the UK and beyond. As a team we have conducted extensive research into how children learn best, and actively apply these principles to our curriculum delivery.
Children arrive at primary school with a real curiosity and zest for learning. They bounce through the doors of nursery or reception with a world of opportunity before them. Our curriculum inspires those young minds to stay curious and keep learning; it shares with them deep and meaningful knowledge, and gives them the courage, confidence and ability to communicate their thoughts, ideas and new learning effectively.
We fully appreciate your support as we work together to educate the citizens of the future. In our welcoming and inclusive school, we strive to be the best in everything we do. Our learners need to develop the knowledge and emotional literacy that will enable them to become fully equipped to cope with the challenges of adult life. Our curriculum reflects this by promoting mental well-being, having high ambition for all and encouraging thinking. Our curriculum has been sequenced logically to give pupils the best possible access to new learning; for example, our historical studies follow a chronological order and our geographical learning starts closest to home and then expands world-wide.
We pride ourselves on:
Quality teaching every day: Learning and equality of opportunity for all is fundamental at Perivale. We promote a collaborative learning model, where children teach and learn from each other, leading to a deeper understanding of content. We prioritise the development of teachers’ expertise, so they can support all our pupils to make significant progress. Teachers know their children extremely well and when any pupil falls behind, they go the extra mile to provide the support needed.
Reading at the heart of the curriculum: Reading is at the heart of our curriculum because we know that the child who excels in reading will excel across the whole curriculum. We strive to nurture lifelong readers who take pleasure in reading everything from literary classics to exciting new fiction and non-fiction works which inspire curiosity in the world.
Strong curriculum design: We provide a culturally rich and vibrant programme of learning. We continually establish cross-curricular links to give cohesion across units of work, and each subject contains carefully chosen skills, knowledge and vocabulary to expand children’s experience and thinking potential – as outlined in our curriculum overviews and progression maps. Our lessons are well taught and appropriately sequenced, and we provide both scaffolding and deepening opportunities to ensure the success of learners of all abilities.
Enrichment and outdoor learning: We supplement our core curriculum with frequent local trips, workshops and visits. These culturally rich experiences enhance our children’s learning and make a marked difference to all areas of the curriculum once back in the classroom. We also endeavour to take learning outside into our extensive grounds as often as we can.
Our cultural values: Threaded throughout our school and revisited continuously are our cultural values:
Through their promotion, teachers develop pupils’ self-esteem and resilience as they progress through school, ensuring our children delight in challenges, strengthen their imagination and become risk takers who do not fear failure.
Resilient
Respectful
Inclusive

Impact & Assessment
Effective assessment provides key information to improve teaching and learning. We have a rigorous progress and target setting model, and base our lesson plans on a detailed knowledge of each pupil’s progress and attainment.
We provide children with regular feedback on their learning so that they understand what they need to do to improve. We also give parents/carers regular reports on their child’s progress so that teachers, children and parents/carers can all work together to raise standards for all our children.

The Importance of Extra-Curricular Opportunities at Our School
We understand that education is not confined to the four walls of a classroom. Providing students with a wide range of extra-curricular activities is essential for their holistic development. These opportunities allow children to explore their interests, develop new skills, and build lasting friendships.
Holistic Development: Extra-curricular activities play a crucial role in nurturing the physical, emotional, and social growth of our students. Whether it’s through sports, arts, or clubs, these activities help children develop a well-rounded personality.
Skill Enhancement: Participating in various activities allows students to discover and hone their talents. From teamwork and leadership in sports to creativity and critical thinking in arts and science clubs, these experiences equip children with valuable life skills.
Building Confidence: Engaging in extra-curricular activities helps students build self-esteem and confidence. Performing in a school play, competing in a sports event, or presenting a science project can boost their confidence and encourage them to take on new challenges.
Social Connections: Extra-curricular activities provide a platform for students to interact with their peers in a relaxed and enjoyable environment. These interactions foster teamwork, communication, and the development of strong social bonds.
Balanced Lifestyle: Encouraging students to participate in activities outside of academics promotes a balanced lifestyle. It helps them manage stress, stay active, and maintain a healthy mind and body.
We are committed to providing a wide array of extracurricular activities that motivate and captivate our students, fostering their development into well-rounded individuals prepared to face the world. Continue browsing our website to learn more about our extracurricular offerings.

Educational Visits at Perivale Primary School
At Perivale, we believe that learning extends beyond the classroom. Our educational visits are designed to provide students with hands-on experiences that enrich their understanding of the world around them. From exploring local museums and historical sites to engaging in nature walks and science centers, our educational visits are carefully planned to complement our curriculum and ignite curiosity.
Benefits of Educational Visits:
We ensure that each visit is safe, enjoyable, and educational, leaving lasting memories and inspiring a lifelong love of learning.
Examples of Educational Visits:
Parents have given permission for local walks, and we will always advise when we are taking pupils out on these walks. For all other educational visits, parents and carers will be asked for permission. In most cases, we will request a voluntary contribution towards the cost of the event or educational visit. However, your child will not be excluded if you are unable to contribute. Please discuss any concerns you have regarding this with your child’s teacher.
We ensure that each visit is safe, enjoyable, and educational, leaving lasting memories and inspiring a lifelong love of learning.
Join us as a parent volunteer on our next adventure and see the world through the eyes of our young explorers!
